title: A Vector for the Static
premise: Noor Fairweather, a xenolinguist stranded on the forgotten colony of Meridian's Rest, discovers their own dreams have been overwritten by an alien signal buried in the colony's failing reactor. When a name that shouldn't exist appears on the manifest of a ship that never launched, Noor uncovers evidence of a massacre the corporate archive has erased entirely. Racing the reactor's countdown, Noor and a handful of invisible colonists broadcast the truth in a language no human was meant to speak, forcing the corporation to acknowledge what it destroyed. In the end, Noor chooses to stay with the colony's survivors, no longer dreaming in any human language but finally belonging to something real.
about_author: Paloma Okonkwo is a former field linguist who spent six years documenting dying languages across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes about people the record forgot, from a small apartment full of archived cassette tapes.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: Noor records the colony's decay, noting their dreams have stopped being human. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: lonely vigilance, the first hint that something is listening back.

chapters.title: Manifest of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Auditing shipping records, Noor finds the name 'Ilya Voss' on a vessel that never flew, dated after the colony's supposed last contact. POV: Noor. Beat: unease sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Introduction of the holdouts: mechanic Sefa, old priest Amara, and teenage scavenger Dex, each with reasons not to leave. POV: rotating. Beat: fragile community warmth.

chapters.title: What the Archive Says
chapters.summary: Noor requests official records and receives flawless documents proving nothing ever happened here. The perfection itself becomes the clue. POV: Noor. Beat: gaslit dread.

chapters.title: Voss, Alive
chapters.summary: Dex finds Ilya Voss living feral in the underlevels, mute and terrified, drawing the same symbols Noor dreams. POV: Dex. Beat: shock and pity.

chapters.title: The Language Under Language
chapters.summary: Noor begins decoding Voss's drawings, realizing they map a night eleven years ago when two hundred colonists vanished. POV: Noor. Beat: terrible recognition.

chapters.title: Reactor Heart
chapters.summary: Sefa reveals the reactor is on an unauthorized countdown nobody programmed. Corporate retrieval ships are inbound. POV: Sefa. Beat: ticking clock established.

chapters.title: Erasure Protocol
chapters.summary: A corporate auditor arrives to 'decommission' the colony, offering Noor a comfortable extraction in exchange for silence. POV: Noor. Beat: temptation and refusal.

chapters.title: Amara's Confession
chapters.summary: The priest admits she helped falsify the original manifest to protect survivors, believing she was saving lives. POV: Amara. Beat: guilt as burden shared.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Names
chapters.summary: Noor reconstructs the victims' names from dialect fragments in Voss's drawings, giving the dead back their identities. POV: Noor. Beat: grief transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: Signal in the Static
chapters.summary: Noor realizes the alien signal in their dreams is a recording of the massacre, preserved by something that witnessed it. POV: Noor. Beat: awe entangled with horror.

chapters.title: The Auditor's Patience Ends
chapters.summary: Corporate forces begin seizing colonists for 'evacuation.' Dex disappears during a raid. POV: Sefa. Beat: fear hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: Underground Chorus
chapters.summary: The holdouts plan to hijack the colony's ancient broadcast array, but it only works if someone can speak the signal language aloud. POV: rotating. Beat: desperate hope.

chapters.title: What Noor Dreams Now
chapters.summary: Noor surrenders fully to the alien signal, learning its grammar at the cost of their remaining human interiority. POV: Noor. Beat: sacrifice of self.

chapters.title: Dex Returns
chapters.summary: Dex escapes custody carrying stolen archive shards proving the corporation ordered the massacre. POV: Dex. Beat: courage rewarded, barely.

chapters.title: Countdown: Forty Hours
chapters.summary: With the reactor near critical, the team races to splice the archive shards into the broadcast array. Sabotage strikes. POV: Sefa. Beat: everything breaking at once.

chapters.title: Amara's Atonement
chapters.summary: Amara sacrifices herself to repair the array under fire, buying the others time. POV: Amara. Beat: redemption through loss.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Noor speaks the massacre into every open channel in a language no human can deny hearing. The galaxy listens. POV: Noor. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: The auditor's superiors arrive to contain the scandal; justice arrives not as law but as exposure. Voss testifies in drawings. POV: rotating. Beat: vindication without comfort.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: The reactor is stabilized by corporate engineers now bound to the colony's survival. Some colonists leave; most stay. POV: Sefa. Beat: exhausted relief.

chapters.title: Dreams Without Words
chapters.summary: Noor mourns the languages they've lost and accepts the self they've become, teaching Voss's symbols to the children. POV: Noor. Beat: quiet transformation.

chapters.title: Meridian's Rest
chapters.summary: One year later, the colony broadcasts openly. Noor adds two hundred names to a memorial wall and finally sleeps without dreaming at all. POV: Noor. Beat: belonging, earned.
